cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: chi-squared test of independence on a 3x2 agree/neutral/disagree by men/women table
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.0003082 and states the underlying statistic is 16.16957 with 2 degrees of freedom. Both figures were re-derived independently: sum over cells of (A-E)^2/E for the documented 3x2 tables gives 16.16957507479688, and with df = (r-1)*(c-1) = (3-1)*(2-1) = 2 the right-tail probability is scipy.stats.chi2.sf(16.16957507479688, 2) = 0.0003081920170083095 -> 0.0003082 at 7 dp

cases.description: Actual and expected ranges identical, so the chi-squared statistic is exactly 0
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that the statistic "is 0 only if Aij = Eij for every i,j". With a statistic of 0 on 2 degrees of freedom the right-tail probability is exactly 1: scipy.stats.chi2.sf(0, 2) = 1.0. This case checks the documented statistic definition at its degenerate point without depending on any published figure

cases.description: Actual and expected ranges with different numbers of data points
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If actual_range and expected_range have a different number of data points, CHITEST returns the #N/A error value." Here the actual range holds 6 values and the expected range 4

cases.description: Single-cell actual and expected ranges, i.e. r = c = 1
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "r = c= 1 is not allowed and #N/A is returned." With one row and one column there are no degrees of freedom left after conditioning on the margins, so CHITEST has no distribution to evaluate
